h: Howay, then: tips for a Toon round
p: A few handy pointers first. Allow around an hour for a round, longer if your group is big or you're the type to retake every shot until you're happy. Get there a little early, and if you're coming as part of a big night out, sort the golf first while everyone can still putt in a straight line. It makes for a much better scorecard and far fewer arguments.

Newcastle has a lot more history than people sometimes expect. The city takes its name from the castle built by the Normans, and the surviving keep and Black Gate sit right in the centre, close to the station. Hadrian's Wall began at Wallsend, a few miles east, where the Segedunum Roman fort and museum mark its eastern end. Fans of a good bake might like to know Greggs started life in Newcastle too.

With kids in tow, the Life Science Centre near Central Station is a hands-on science attraction that fills a few hours easily, while the Discovery Museum and the Great North Museum: Hancock are both great for curious minds. Football fans will spot St James' Park looming over the city, home of Newcastle United.

And if the sun does come out, jump on the Metro to the coast. Tynemouth, with its priory ruins and sandy Longsands beach, and Whitley Bay, with its seafront and St Mary's Lighthouse, both make cracking add-ons to a day of putting.
